source.title: Towards harnessing feature embedding for robust learning with noisy labels
source.authors: Chuang Zhang; Li Shen; Jian Yang; Chen Gong

record.file_problem: none; the supplied text contains the full paper and appendix.
record.tranche_reason: It measures learning under noisy labels using feature visualizations, label accuracies, and test-accuracy curves rather than the original random-label fitting experiment.
record.gate_note: The paper tests learning of clean versus noisy labels over training. It does not test completely random labels, zero training error on random labels, shuffled or Gaussian inputs, explicit regularization, or fitting-time comparisons. Results cited from Arpit et al. are not extracted as this study’s results.
record.test_reason: The study's own standard-training experiments bear on V6: early representations align with true classes, later representations fit noisy labels, and test accuracy rises before declining as training continues. LEND's performance comparisons alone do not test the claim.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors conclude that early feature embeddings are more robust to label noise than classifier predictions, and that LEND exploits this property to improve noisy-label learning.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses asymmetric or symmetric label corruption and analyzes embeddings, label accuracy, and test accuracy; it does not use the original completely random-label fitting experiment.
record.method_sensitivity: The plotted Standard test-accuracy trajectory is reported for multiple noise types and rates; the feature-embedding visualizations use 45% asymmetric noise, while the diluted-label comparison uses 40% asymmetric noise.

fits_no_version.finding: Diluted labels are substantially more accurate than model-predicted labels under 40% asymmetric CIFAR-10 noise.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Feature-based label dilution can recover true labels more accurately than the network's classifier predictions.

record.problems: The evidence for learning order is largely qualitative or presented in figures; the text gives no numerical training-error results for random labels. The reported experiments use structured asymmetric or symmetric corruption, not fully random labels.

untested.parts: Completely random labels, near-zero training error, chance test performance, and fitting without architecture or hyperparameter changes.
Relative training time for true and random labels, and convergence slowdown as corruption increases.
Fitting shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, or Gaussian-noise inputs.
Perfect training fit across corruption rates and a full corruption sweep from clean labels to chance-level test performance. Reported test accuracies alone do not establish this joint behavior.
Whether explicit regularizers prevent random-label fitting and whether removing them impairs true-label generalization.
Completely random-label training and a separate comparison of wholly clean versus wholly random datasets; direct quantitative clean-subset and corrupted-subset fitting curves.

missing.what: Standard ResNet-18 on CIFAR-100 also has lower final than best test accuracy. Under symmetric noise of 40%, 50%, and 60%, best/final-ten-epoch means are 43.75/33.24, 36.92/21.80, and 25.71/15.33 percent. Under asymmetric noise of 20%, 30%, and 40%, they are 42.97/41.52, 35.53/34.29, and 30.89/29.43 percent. These provide additional indirect evidence of late generalization deterioration, although they do not directly measure clean-versus-noisy fitting order.

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source. Symmetric corruption is randomly generated, contrary to the record's blanket statement that the experiments do not use random labels; however, no experiment uses completely random labeling of the entire training set. The supplied text supports qualitative trajectory judgments, but its figure images do not provide readable numerical curves.

versions.untested_parts: Completely random training labels, zero or near-zero training error, chance test error, and unchanged architecture and hyperparameters.
Training-time comparison between true and random labels and convergence time as corruption increases.
Shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, and Gaussian-noise inputs.
Perfect training fit across corruption rates and steadily rising test error through fully random labels.
Whether weight decay, dropout, or augmentation prevent random-label fitting or whether removing them harms true-label generalization.
The paper studies asymmetric and synthetic label noise, not random labels; it does not separately compare learning under true labels alone with learning under random labels.

rows.subject: ResNet-18
rows.operation_detail: t-SNE visualization of last-hidden-layer embeddings and model-predicted labels during training on noisy CIFAR-10
rows.measure: Embedding clusters relative to ground-truth labels; prediction accuracy described qualitatively
rows.value: The text says same-ground-truth-label points cluster together while model predictions still make errors.
rows.note: Qualitative result; no numerical accuracy is given.
rows.check: Qualitative evidence for the early signal-learning phase, interpreted together with R3. Prediction errors do not make V6 partial: it does not require perfect early predictions.

rows.subject: ResNet-18
rows.operation_detail: t-SNE visualization of last-hidden-layer embeddings and model-predicted labels during training on noisy CIFAR-10
rows.measure: Embedding quality relative to ground-truth labels
rows.value: The authors state that early-stage embeddings are good with respect to ground-truth labels.
rows.note: The appendix identifies these visualizations as early-stage evidence; no numerical measure is reported.
rows.check: Early ground-truth-aligned representations support the first phase of V6 when paired with R3. Qualitative measurement alone does not justify a partial state.

source_check.locator_found: Appendix Section 7, observation (3); Figures 9 and 10 captions, pp. 23–24.

rows.subject: ResNet-18
rows.operation_detail: t-SNE visualization of last-hidden-layer embeddings during training on noisy CIFAR-10
rows.measure: Embedding quality relative to noisy labels
rows.value: The authors state that DNNs gradually fit noisy labels and ultimately form a good embedding with respect to noisy labels.
rows.note: Qualitative result, with the paper defining a good embedding as pulling same-label examples together and pushing different-label examples apart.
rows.check: The appendix explicitly describes eventual fitting of noisy labels at 200 epochs. This supplies the later phase of the trajectory documented by R1 and R2; it does not establish zero training error.

source_check.locator_found: Appendix Section 7, observation (1) and embedding-definition footnote; Figure 12 caption, pp. 23–24.

rows.subject: ResNet-18, Standard
rows.operation_detail: Test-accuracy curves during training on noisy CIFAR-10
rows.value: The text says Standard first reaches a very high test accuracy as the DNN first fits clean labels, then overfits noisy labels and its test accuracy decreases.
rows.note: The statement summarizes plotted curves across the listed noise settings; no numerical values are stated in the text.
rows.check: The authors explicitly describe clean-label learning followed by noisy-label overfitting across these conditions. Noisy rather than completely random labels are within V6; this distinction does not warrant limits_scope. The curves summarize five trials with standard deviations.

source_check.locator_found: Sections 5.2 and 5.3, Standard definition, implementation details and Results on CIFAR-10; Figures 6 and 7 captions, pp. 12–14.

rows.subject: ResNet-18
rows.operation_detail: Accuracy comparison of diluted labels and model-predicted labels during training
rows.measure: Accuracy of diluted labels versus model-predicted labels
rows.value: The text says diluted-label accuracy outperforms model-predicted-label accuracy by a large margin.
rows.note: The text describes the plotted comparison but does not state numerical values.
rows.check: Diluted-label accuracy versus prediction accuracy measures the effectiveness of the authors' feature-based correction method, not the order of learning signal and noise. It should not be a claim-testing row.

relationships.condition: Standard ResNet-18 on CIFAR-10 with 45% asymmetric noise, from 30 through 200 epochs
relationships.reason: R1 and R2 describe early representations aligned with true classes; R3 describes eventual fitting of noisy labels, supporting the claimed learning order qualitatively.
relationships.display_finding: Early representations aligned with true classes before the network eventually fit noisy labels.
